  "text": "Everyone looked at the ceiling except Anne.

“That's not a bed,” she said.

The boy's mother released him, leaving four white places on his wrist. He slipped his hand into his pocket. There was a rubber, a penny, and the small plastic foot of a toy he couldn't picture.

“Where's my bag?”

“Under the stairs,” said the younger father.

“Don't answer him,” the older one said.

But the boy had already opened the cupboard.

His bag hung from its hook. The buckles were fastened, though he never fastened them. Beneath it stood a pair of yellow swimming fins, each filled to the ankle with dark water.

He lifted the bag carefully over them.

Upstairs, the scraping stopped.

“Let me see the label,” his mother said.

He hugged the bag against his chest. Suddenly he disliked the way they were all waiting for him to open it.

Anne reached out, then put her hand flat on the floor instead.

“You can keep it shut,” she said.

The letter box lifted behind the older father's knees.

“Have you got his towel?” a woman called.

His mother made a sound he had only heard once before, when she shut her finger in the car door.

The younger father knelt beside the swimming fins. He dipped one finger into the water and brought it to his mouth.

“Salt,” he said.

From inside the schoolbag came the muffled ring of a telephone.

The boy felt someone shift their weight on the other side of the canvas.

Then his own voice said, very politely, “Please can I come home now?”"
